name: Crater Ridge
geological_features: Overlapping impact craters whose raised rims form continuous ridge systems
Ejecta blankets of mixed rock types
Central peak formations in the largest craters
specific_features: A crater ridge used as the foundation for a relay communications array
description: Crater Ridge is a small, airless barren world whose surface has been so thoroughly cratered that the raised rims of overlapping impacts form continuous ridge systems across the terrain. Walking the surface means traversing an endless series of crater walls, each ridge leading to the next in a chaotic topography of concentric circles. The largest craters feature central peaks thrust upward by the energy of ancient impacts.

Without atmosphere, the ridges cast razor-sharp shadows across the crater floors. The ejecta blankets create a mosaic of different rock types, each impact having excavated material from different depths and scattered it across the surface. The visual effect is of a world assembled from fragments, a geological collage of violence and time.

Crater Ridge's impact history spans billions of years, and its surface is effectively a record of the local debris environment over that period. Impact frequency analysis suggests the body passed through a particularly dense debris field approximately five hundred million years ago, which accounts for the heaviest cratering. Its current orbit is more sedate.

A communications relay array has been constructed along one of the highest ridge systems, taking advantage of the elevation and the body's strategic position in the system. The relay station is the only permanent installation, staffed by a small maintenance crew. Crater Ridge's minerals are accessible but not remarkable enough to justify dedicated mining, and the body's primary value remains its position rather than its substance.
